findings.statement: A compact species/duration/digital-amplitude equation transfers source context-label prediction to held animals

reliability.rationale: Held-animal Brier0.190215 beats species0.205977 and flexible0.201616; scope is experimental context classification. Claim-specific scope: A compact species/duration/digital-amplitude equation transfers source context-label prediction to held animals

mechanism.rationale: Uncalibrated digital amplitude and duration can encode recorder, call type or eliciting context. Animal holdout cannot isolate an emotional physiological mechanism.

novelty.rationale: Primary-source analyses and established equation families are disclosed. This review does not establish exhaustive literature novelty or a new universal law.

significance.rationale: Useful as a transparent bounded research/evaluation case. Seven species with study/context/recording confounding; WildBoar spelling linkage audited; subjective valence and deployed welfare decisions unmeasured.

reproducibility.rationale: Exact task, equation/state, group evidence, native semantics and provenance inspected; separate computational review is responsible for complete replay.

impact.rationale: No independent deployment, intervention, cost saving or clinical/industrial acceptance outcome was measured.

reliability.rationale: All saved predictions and primary metrics independently reproduce from source-verified inputs, including unfavorable alternatives. Held-animal recorded-context Brier comparison favors the selected acoustic descriptor, but species/recording/context confounding prevents interpreting it as directly measured emotional state or animal-welfare impact.
